triage.summary: Capacity plan for message queue at 4.2k msg/s with 3x burst

plan.plan:
CAPACITY PLAN - Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) message queue at 4,200 msg/s peak with 3x burst allowance (12,600 msg/s)

STEP 0 - Canonical parameters and labeled assumptions (single source of truth; every later step reuses these values verbatim)
- Technology: Apache Kafka on Amazon MSK. A broker = one MSK broker node = one Kafka broker process (process.roles=broker per Kafka docs). MSK operates the controller quorum separately; only broker nodes are counted and billed.
- Peak sustained ingress: 4,200 msg/s (per triage, the non-burst rate the system must sustain).
- Burst allowance: 3x peak = 12,600 msg/s, sustainable up to 15 minutes per burst, at most 4 bursts/day, aggregate <= 1 hour/day. This definition is used identically in sizing (Steps 1-5), cost (Step 6), and operations (Step 7).
- Average on-wire message size: 2 KiB (2,048 bytes) including key, headers, payload, and protocol framing. ASSUMPTION - not verified in sources; recompute rule in Step 9.
- Max message size: 1 MiB (message.max.bytes = 1,048,576).
- Retention: 72 h time-based (retention.ms = 259,200,000) plus a per-partition size backstop (Step 3).
- Durability: replication.factor = 3, min.insync.replicas = 2, producer acks = all with enable.idempotence = true -> zero data loss on any single-broker failure; at-least-once delivery semantics.
- Consumers: 2 consumer groups each reading the full stream; each group must sustain 12,600 msg/s aggregate so lag stays bounded during bursts.
- Geography: single region, 3 AZs, 2 brokers per AZ. Multi-region DR out of scope (future option: MirrorMaker 2).
- Redundancy: N+1 - the cluster must serve the full 12,600 msg/s burst with one broker failed (verified in Step 5).
- Currency: USD. Prices are us-east-1 list prices, ASSUMPTIONS to verify at procurement.
- Planning horizon: 12 months, sized to the stated peak with no growth allowance; review at 6 months or on any Step 7 capacity alert.
- Security baseline: TLS in transit, SASL/IAM auth, encryption at rest (MSK defaults) - no capacity impact.

STEP 1 - Throughput derivation (sizing basis)
- Sustained logical ingress: 4,200 msg/s x 2 KiB = 8,400 KiB/s = 8.2 MiB/s.
- Burst logical ingress: 12,600 msg/s x 2 KiB = 25,200 KiB/s = 24.6 MiB/s.
- Cluster physical write rate at RF=3: sustained 3 x 8.2 = 24.6 MiB/s; burst 3 x 24.6 = 73.8 MiB/s.
- Consumer egress (2 groups): sustained 2 x 8.2 = 16.4 MiB/s; burst 2 x 24.6 = 49.2 MiB/s.
- Sizing deliberately ignores producer compression (conservative; lz4 typically adds 30-60% effective headroom).

STEP 2 - Broker count and instance type
- Deploy 6 brokers of kafka.m5.xlarge (4 vCPU, 16 GiB RAM), 2 per AZ across 3 AZs.
- Per-broker load at the full 12,600 msg/s burst with 6 healthy brokers: 8 leader partitions; producer ingress 24.6/6 = 4.1 MiB/s; replication fetch in 8.2 MiB/s; disk write 73.8/6 = 12.3 MiB/s; consumer + replication egress 8.2 + 8.2 = 16.4 MiB/s; total network ~28.7 MiB/s ~ 241 Mbit/s = 24% of the 1 Gbit/s per-broker planning envelope.
- Estimated CPU at burst <= 40% of 4 vCPU (TLS + protocol work at ~29 MiB/s combined), below the 65% warning threshold in Step 7.
- Trade-off considered: 3 x kafka.m5.2xlarge has identical compute cost ($0.42/hr x 3 = $0.21/hr x 6) but leaves ~723 Mbit/s per broker (72% of the envelope) during a broker failure and halves failure granularity; rejected. With 6 brokers, per-broker burst load stays at 24% of the envelope and leadership is even (8 leaders per broker).

STEP 3 - Topic and partition configuration
- Primary topic 'events': 48 partitions (divisible by 6 brokers and 3 AZs -> 8 leaders per broker, even AZ spread).
- Per-partition rate at burst: 12,600/48 = 262.5 msg/s = 0.51 MiB/s; 48 partitions also let a consumer group scale to 48 instances (~262 msg/s each at burst).
- Topic configs: replication.factor=3; min.insync.replicas=2; retention.ms=259200000 (72 h); retention.bytes=85899345920 (80 GiB per partition) as a disk-safety backstop; max.message.bytes=1048576; segment.bytes=1073741824.
- Backstop consistency check: 48 partitions x 80 GiB x RF 3 = 11,520 GiB < 12,000 GiB provisioned (Step 4), so the size backstop can never overfill the cluster.
- Producer settings: acks=all, enable.idempotence=true, linger.ms=20, batch.size=65536, compression.type=lz4.

STEP 4 - Storage sizing
- Daily logical volume at sustained peak: 8.2 MiB/s x 86,400 s = 692 GiB/day.
- Burst extra: (12,600 - 4,200) msg/s x 2 KiB x 3,600 s/day = 57.7 GiB/day logical (from the 1 h/day aggregate burst).
- 72-h physical volume: (692 + 57.7) GiB/day x 3 days x RF 3 = ~6,748 GiB cluster = ~1,125 GiB per broker expected steady state.
- Provision 2,000 GiB per broker (12,000 GiB cluster): steady state 56%; headroom covers index files and re-replication after a broker loss (worst case 1,125 + 225 = 1,350 GiB = 68%, still below the 70% disk warning in Step 7).

STEP 5 - Failure-mode (N+1) verification
- 1 broker down (5 remain): per-broker burst write 73.8/5 = 14.8 MiB/s; total network ~34.4 MiB/s ~ 289 Mbit/s (29% of the envelope) -> the full 12,600 msg/s burst is still served.
- RF=3 + min.insync.replicas=2: with 1 broker down every partition keeps ISR >= 2, so acks=all produce continues with zero data loss.
- 2 brokers down in the same AZ: ISR >= 2 still holds (one replica per AZ) -> writes continue; this is the critical alert condition in Step 7 because a further failure in another AZ would halt acks=all produce.

STEP 6 - Cost model (per broker, USD/month)
- Broker compute: kafka.m5.xlarge at $0.21/hr (us-east-1 list price, ASSUMPTION - verify) x 730 h = $153.30 per broker-month.
- Broker storage: 2,000 GB x $0.10/GB-month (list price, ASSUMPTION - verify) = $200.00 per broker-month.
- Per-broker total: $353.30/month. Cluster of 6: $2,119.80/month (compute $919.80 + storage $1,200.00).
- Cross-AZ data transfer (cluster-level, derived from the same throughput figures): replication moves 2x every produced byte across AZs -> sustained 2 x 8.2 MiB/s plus burst extra 2 x 16.4 MiB/s for 1 h/day = ~48.3 TB/month ~ $483; consumer fetches (2 groups, 2/3 crossing AZ) ~32.2 TB/month ~ $322; total ~$805/month at $0.01/GB (ASSUMPTION: rate charged once per byte; if charged at both ends it is ~$1,610 - verify).
- Cluster total: $2,119.80 + $805 = ~$2,925/month = ~$35,100/year. No license cost (open-source Kafka; MSK is priced per broker-hour plus storage).
- The burst allowance is included in this cost: the 1 h/day aggregate burst produces the 57.7 GiB/day storage extra (Step 4) and the burst-extra transfer lines above; removing the burst allowance would lower storage + transfer by ~8%.

STEP 7 - Operations: monitoring and alert thresholds (all derived from the sizing design points)
Metric sources: MSK CloudWatch per-broker metrics (CPUUser, KafkaDataLogsDiskUsed, NetworkProcessorAvgIdlePercent, RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent, UnderReplicatedPartitions, OfflinePartitionsCount, BytesInPerSec, BytesOutPerSec - confirm exact metric names during implementation); consumer lag = (latest offset - committed offset) / current ingress rate; produce and consume p99 latency from client-side metrics. MSK exposes no direct per-broker disk-IOPS metric: I/O pressure is caught by alerts 9 and 13. No static memory threshold: Kafka page cache is expected to fill RAM; investigate memory only alongside latency alerts.

Alerts (warning / critical):
1. Cluster produce ingress (msg/s = sum(BytesInPerSec) / 2,048 - the same 2 KiB used for sizing): WARN > 12,600 msg/s for 10 min (burst allowance exceeded); CRIT > 12,600 for 30 min, or > 18,900 (1.5x burst) for 5 min.
2. Sustained load growth: WARN > 5,250 msg/s (125% of the 4,200 planned peak) for 30 min -> open a capacity review.
3. Broker CPU: WARN >= 65% for 15 min; CRIT >= 80% for 5 min. Expected <= 40% at full burst.
4. Per-broker network: WARN >= 600 Mbit/s (60% of the 1 Gbit/s envelope) for 10 min; CRIT >= 800 Mbit/s for 5 min. Expected 241 Mbit/s at burst, 289 Mbit/s with one broker down.
5. Disk usage per broker: WARN >= 70% (1,400 GiB); CRIT >= 80% (1,600 GiB); EMERGENCY >= 90% (1,800 GiB) -> page + runbook R-3. Expected steady 1,125 GiB (56%); worst-case re-replication 1,350 GiB (68%).
6. Under-replicated partitions: WARN > 0 for 5 min; CRIT > 0 for 15 min.
7. Offline partitions: CRIT > 0 for 1 min (immediate page - availability incident).
8. Broker availability: WARN 1 broker down > 5 min; CRIT >= 2 brokers down > 1 min (acks=all produce at risk).
9. Produce p99 latency: WARN > 150 ms for 5 min; CRIT > 400 ms for 5 min. Targets: <= 50 ms sustained, <= 100 ms at burst; alerts sit >= 50% above targets so healthy bursts never page.
10. Consumer lag (time-based): WARN > 60 s for 5 min; CRIT > 300 s for 5 min. Message equivalents at the canonical rates: 60 s = 252,000 msgs at 4,200 msg/s; 756,000 msgs at 12,600 msg/s.
11. Post-burst lag drain: after ingress falls back below 4,200 msg/s, lag must drop under 10 s within 15 min; WARN if it does not (consumer fleet not keeping up with burst).
12. End-to-end consume p99: WARN > 750 ms for 10 min; CRIT > 1,500 ms for 10 min. Targets: <= 200 ms sustained, <= 500 ms at burst.
13. Request handler avg idle and network processor avg idle: WARN < 30% for 5 min; CRIT < 10% for 5 min.

STEP 8 - Runbook actions tied to the alerts
- R-1 (alert 8 WARN, 1 broker down): confirm MSK node replacement; verify under-replicated partitions return to 0 within 15 min; no capacity action needed - N+1 covers the full burst (Step 5).
- R-2 (alerts 6-7): check for an AZ event; with 2 brokers down treat as CRIT; acks=all producers will error while ISR < 2 on affected partitions.
- R-3 (alert 5, disk >= 70%): expand MSK broker storage online (e.g., +500 GiB per broker ~ +$50/broker-month at $0.10/GB-month); check alerts 1-2 for ingress above plan.
- R-4 (alert 1, ingress > 12,600 sustained): capacity breach - apply producer-side rate limiting at 12,600 msg/s while the Step 9 re-plan runs.
- R-5 (alerts 10-11, lag): scale the consumer group toward its 48-instance ceiling (~262 msg/s per instance at burst).
- Maintenance: rolling patches one broker at a time are safe at any time (N+1); never take a second broker down while under-replicated partitions > 0.

STEP 9 - Recompute rules if assumptions are corrected (keeps the plan valid without redesign)
- If the measured average message size is S KiB instead of 2: ingress MiB/s = rate x S / 1024; per-broker burst network ~ 14.35 x S MiB/s; if S > 4 KiB this passes ~48% of the 1 Gbit/s envelope and approaches the 60% warning line -> re-run Step 2 (more brokers or a larger instance). Storage scales linearly: provision ~1,000 x S GiB per broker to hold the 56% steady point (S=4 -> 4,000 GiB -> $400/broker-month storage).
- If the burst duty cycle exceeds 1 h/day aggregate, recompute Step 4 storage and Step 6 transfer linearly with burst hours.
- If sustained peak exceeds 5,250 msg/s (alert 2) or growth is confirmed, re-run Steps 1-6 ahead of the 6-month review.

STEP 10 - Cross-section consistency checklist (apply before publishing)
- 4,200 / 12,600 / 3x appear identically in sizing (Steps 1-2), cost (Step 6 burst lines), and operations (alerts 1, 2, 10, 11).
- 2 KiB appears in sizing (Step 1), the operations ingress conversion (alert 1), and the lag equivalents (alert 10).
- 8.2 / 24.6 / 73.8 MiB/s, 6 brokers, 48 partitions, 2,000 GiB provisioned, 1,125 GiB steady, $353.30 per broker-month, $2,925/month - each value appears with one number everywhere it is used.
- The cost_estimate field of this plan = USD 2,925 per month (~USD 35,100 per year).
success_criteria: The sizing section derives sustained ingress of 8.2 MiB/s from 4,200 msg/s x 2 KiB and burst ingress of 24.6 MiB/s from 12,600 msg/s x 2 KiB, and these exact figures (8.2, 24.6, 73.8 MiB/s) reappear unchanged in the cost section's data-transfer derivation and in the operations section's alert baselines.

The sizing section specifies exactly 6 kafka.m5.xlarge brokers with 2,000 GiB provisioned storage each and a 48-partition topic (8 leaders per broker), and the cost section prices those same 6 brokers at $353.30 per broker per month ($153.30 compute at $0.21/hr x 730 h plus $200.00 storage at 2,000 GB x $0.10/GB-month), totaling $2,119.80/month before data transfer.

The operations section's thresholds are numerically derived from the sizing design points: disk alerts at 70/80/90% of 2,000 GiB (1,400/1,600/1,800 GiB) sit above the stated 1,125 GiB (56%) steady state and 1,350 GiB (68%) worst-case re-replication; network alerts at 600/800 Mbit/s sit above the stated 241 Mbit/s per-broker burst load; and the ingress alert fires above 12,600 msg/s.

The 3x burst allowance of 12,600 msg/s is explicitly reflected in all three required sections: sizing (burst design point plus the N+1 check that 5 brokers still serve 12,600 msg/s), cost (the 1 hour/day aggregate burst included in the 57.7 GiB/day storage extra and the cross-AZ transfer lines), and operations (the burst-exceeded alert at >12,600 msg/s and the post-burst lag-drain rule).

Every unverified input - the 2 KiB average message size, 72-hour retention, $0.21/hr broker price, $0.10/GB-month storage price, 1 hour/day burst duty cycle, and $0.01/GB cross-AZ rate - is labeled as an assumption in the plan and covered by a stated recompute rule that scales the affected figures.

The plan includes a cross-section consistency checklist, and no figure that appears in more than one section (message rates, byte rates, broker count, partition count, storage, prices) takes a conflicting value anywhere in the document.
